title: Finite-dimensional cohomology of a finite supported complex
statement: Let $E$ be a field and $K$ a cochain complex of $E$-vector spaces. Suppose $S\subset\mathbf Z$ is finite, $K^i=0$ for $i\notin S$, and every $K^i$ is finite-dimensional. Then the image $Q(K)$ in the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] has cohomology supported in $S$, and every cohomology vector space is finite-dimensional; thus it belongs to $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E)$ as defined in [def-weil-point-fd-complexes].

source.place: Coefficient-point comparison, finite models in steps 3 and 5 of lem-zl-condensed-point-supertrace

proof.text: Outside S the middle term of the short complex computing H^i(K) is zero, so its homology is zero. Transport this fact along the localization homology comparison.

The existing CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.finiteDimensional_homology instance realizes homology as the quotient of the kernel of the outgoing differential by the incoming image. Subspaces and quotients retain finite dimension. Transfer the instance along the same localization comparison.

proof_origin.place: N4: elementary kernel/quotient calculation for the bounded finite-dimensional models
